articles.title: Reuters poll: 37% of Japan firms see oil volatility as biggest risk to earnings
articles.desc: The survey reinforces Japan's acute sensitivity to the Iran war: with almost all crude imports sourced from the Middle East, any further disruption to Gulf shipping (like this), such as this week's tanker attack north of Qatar, feeds directly into corporate costs and margins. That leaves energy-inte
articles.content: The survey reinforces Japan's acute sensitivity to the Iran war: with almost all crude imports sourced from the Middle East, any further disruption to Gulf shipping (like this), such as this week's tanker attack north of Qatar, feeds directly into corporate costs and margins. That leaves energy-intensive sectors such as materials, chemicals, cement and transport most exposed if oil stays elevated, while higher fuel import bills add to pressure on the yen. A tilt towards second-half earnings downgrades could weigh on Japanese equities heading into the results season, particularly if crude stays high and the Bank of Japan keeps tightening. Concerns about the durability of AI spending point to downside risk for chip equipment and data centre suppliers that have led the market. --- Japan Inc's biggest worry is no longer the yen or the Bank of Japan but the price of oil, and it is starting to cloud the profit outlook for the second half of the year. Summary: About 37% of Japanese firms named crude oil market volatility as the top risk to earnings, ahead of foreign exchange moves (21%) and rising interest rates (19%), according to a Reuters survey The Iran war, which began on 28 February, has constrained crude supply and pushed up the cost of energy and oil-derived products; Japan sourced 94% of its crude imports from the Middle East in 2025 Several firms also flagged doubts over how long AI-related investment will last For the first half of the fiscal year, 32% expect net earnings to beat their own forecasts and 22% expect a miss For the October-to-March half, the outlook turns cautious: 22% expect to fall short and 20% expect to beat forecasts The survey of 215 firms was conducted by Nikkei Research for Reuters from 18 September to 2 October Volatility in the global oil market has become the biggest threat to Japanese corporate earnings, ranking ahead of currency fluctuations and rising interest rates, a Reuters survey showed on Thursday. About 37% of respondents identified crude market volatility as the leading risk to their earnings prospects, while 21% chose foreign exchange moves and 19% picked higher interest rates. The poll was conducted by Nikkei Research for Reuters between 18 September and 2 October, with 215 of the 508 companies contacted responding on condition of anonymity. The concern reflects Japan's heavy reliance on imported energy. The country sourced 94% of its crude oil imports from the Middle East in 2025, and the US-Israeli war on Iran, which began on 28 February, has restricted supply and lifted prices for energy and a wide range of oil-based products, including auto parts and construction materials. A ceramics sector manager said rising energy costs, together with investment cutbacks that are cooling domestic cement demand as rates climb, were the key risks facing the business. Higher borrowing costs are a growing theme. The Bank of Japan raised interest rates to a 31-year high last month, and Governor Kazuo Ueda signalled the central bank had entered a new phase focused on preventing inflation from overshooting its target, leaving the door open to further increases. A real estate executive said higher rates were bound to slow property demand. Several respondents also pointed to uncertainty over the durability of investment linked to artificial intelligence, which has driven demand for advanced chips and a rapid expansion of data centres. One machinery maker said it was vital for companies to judge how long the AI-driven boost to demand would last and when it might start to fade. A Tokyo-based think tank said last month that AI investment is likely to grow over the medium to long term, but that power constraints, tighter regulation and rising costs could slow its pace. Near-term results look steadier than the outlook beyond them. For the April-to-September half, 32% of firms expect net earnings to beat their own forecasts, 22% expect to miss and 46% see results in line. For the October-to-March period, however, 22% expect to fall short, slightly more than the 20% expecting to beat, while 58% see their initial forecasts as intact. Half-year earnings announcements begin later this month and run into November, giving the first read on how far energy costs are squeezing margins. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.content: SRX Global and CERO 1236, a Wholly-Owned SPV, Enter into SRX Global and CERO 1236, a Wholly-Owned SPV, Enter into Definitive Agreement to Acquire CERo Therapeutics, an Innovative Cellular Immunotherapy Company Developing CER 1236 for Hematologic Malignancies SPV, CERO 1236, to raise capital directly into subsidiary and not dilute existing SRX Global shareholders Proposed acquisition expected to accelerate development of CERo's lead product candidate, CER-1236, for hematologic malignancies NORTH PALM BEACH, Fla., Oct. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SRX Global Inc. (NYSE American: SRXH) (the “Company” or “SRX”), an AI-enabled platform dedicated to generating long-term shareholder value through investments in high-conviction operating companies and strategic assets, today announced that it has entered into definitive purchase agreement under which CERo Therapeutics, the operating subsidiary of CERo Therapeutics Holdings, Inc. (OTCQB: CERO) ("CERo Holdings" and, together with CERo Therapeutics, "CERo"), an innovative cellular immunotherapy company advancing the next generation of engineered T cell therapeutics that employ phagocytic mechanisms, will become a wholly owned subsidiary of SRX Global. The pending transaction is expected to accelerate the advancement of CERo's clinical programs. The combination of Cero and the CERO 1236 SPV is expected to benefit from enhanced access to capital. The transaction combines SRX Global's public company infrastructure with CERo's innovative oncology platform. Chief Executive Officer of SRX Global Inc., Kent Cunningham stated, "This proposed acquisition reflects our strategy of investing in high-conviction operating companies with meaningful long-term value creation potential. CERo's differentiated approach to engineered T cell therapeutics, and the clinical progress the team has made with CER-1236, make it a compelling addition to our platform. We expect this transaction to give CERo enhanced access to capital and broader operational resources to support continued advancement of CER-1236 and its broader R&D efforts, while providing SRX shareholders exposure to an innovative oncology asset." CERo Chief Executive Officer, Chris Ehrlich added, "This proposed transaction represents an important development for CERo and our mission to develop potentially life-prolonging therapies for patients experiencing rare and difficult-to-treat cancers. By becoming part of SRX, we expect CERo Therapeutics to benefit from broader operational resources that can support the continued advancement of CER-1236 and our broader R&D efforts. We believe the proposed transaction provides a stronger platform from which to execute our clinical development strategy and create long-term value for patients and shareholders." Under the terms of the proposed transaction, Andrew ("Al") Kucharchuk, currently CERo Chief Financial Officer, is expected to serve as President of and primary executive of CERo Therapeutics following the closing of the proposed transaction. Chris Ehrlich and current CERo director Brian Atwood are each expected to serve on the CERo Therapeutics Board of Directors and as Special Advisors to the President. This leadership structure is intended to provide continuity for CERo Therapeutics operations. To date, CERo has reported treating six patients in the ongoing Phase 1 CERTAIN-T trial. In the most recent cohort of three patients, CER-1236 was administered at an increased dose level, with no dose-limiting toxicities ("DLTs") observed during the DLT assessment period. As previously reported, CERo has also observed expansion of infused CER-1236 cells following administration, and CERo continues to evaluate the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profile of CER-1236 as the study advances through dose escalation. These clinical results are preliminary and are not sufficient to establish the safety or efficacy of CER-1236. articles.title: Why Chick-fil-A's view on drive-thru AI is the right one
articles.desc: The Bottom Line: The fast-food chicken-sandwich chain is apparently taking a stand against having AI bots take orders so humans provide the hospitality.
articles.content: Why Chick-fil-A's view on drive-thru AI is the right one How Del Taco is faring under its new owner Chick-fil-A's drive-thrus are busy enough without robots. | Photo: Shutterstock Drive-thru AI remains a major goal for a number of fast-food chains, including two of the four biggest in McDonald’s and Taco Bell. Plenty of industry executives and operators would love to see the technology advance to the point where a robot is the one greeting customers at the drive-thru speaker. Do not, apparently, include Chick-fil-A’s CEO in that group. Andrew Cathy, the CEO of the chicken-sandwich chain, told CNBC that its restaurants will not use AI in its drive-thrus. “From our experience,” he said, “we really want that hospitality to be human to human.” This is the right move. Chick-fil-A has long emphasized hospitality inside its restaurants. No matter how good AI may get in the future, at the end of the day it is still a robot programmed or directed to provide good service. And that is not the same as a human providing that service. Going away from that, and substituting the human order taker for a robot, would go against what has been a fundamental tenet of the Chick-fil-A system, that its workers provide an unusual level of hospitality. They greet customers warmly and say things like “my pleasure” that other brands don’t do. To be sure, Chick-fil-A is not the only chain opting against drive-thru AI. Burger King, for instance, said at the FSTEC conference that it is pumping the brakes on drive-thru AI, largely because a number of consumers don’t like it. Consumers do not like drive-thru AI compared with other ordering channels. According to Restaurant Business sibling company Technomic, 38% of consumers say AI-voiced and AI-powered menu boards would make them visit a restaurant less often, and only 16% said they would visit more often. That makes it one of the least accepted technologies in the drive-thru. Restaurant chains love the concept of drive-thru AI because it could potentially save on labor. At McDonald’s, the technology is a potentially major piece of its “Next” strategy, one that it says could save 50 hours in labor a week. (We give McDonald’s credit, because it is the only company actually willing to say that, while most companies will provide some sort of comment that AI “allows workers to spend more time with customers,” as if taking someone’s order isn’t interacting with customers.) But the fact is, that still makes the technology a visible replacement for humans, and that is bad PR for an industry that doesn’t need such things right now. Drive-thru AI might be able to convince users to buy more and it may well save on labor. But the industry is saturated. Supply of fast-food restaurants exceeds demand, so there are plenty of concepts out there that customers can go to if they don’t like what they’re presented with at a restaurant chain. Customers, in other words, may opt not to go to restaurants with robot order-takers. And there will be plenty of brands to greet them with human beings, such as the burger chain Culver’s or drive-thru drink concepts 7 Brew and Dutch Bros. Chick-fil-A’s business model has enabled an enormous level of growth and incredible throughput at its existing locations. Its average-unit volumes are among the highest in the fast-food industry, and only Portillo’s does more. But Chick-fil-A’s stand-alone units do more than $9 million in sales per year. Why would it need robots to do more of the work? articles.title: Plans submitted for huge data centre in countryside on outskirts of Norwich
articles.desc: Plans for a hugely controversial data centre on the edge of Norwich, near Keswick, have been submitted to South Norfolk Council.
articles.content: Plans for data centre on outskirts of Norwich submitted | Eastern Daily Press Plans for data centre on outskirts of Norwich submitted This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Plans for a controversial data centre in countryside on the outskirts of Norwich have been submitted. Norwich Apex Ltd wants to build a seven-acre (three-hectare) data centre on land at Keswick, off Ipswich Road, opposite the Tesco Harford Bridge superstore. Initial details of the scheme sparked anger across the city and South Norfolk, with almost 15,000 people signing a petition against it. Daniel Elmer, the leader of South Norfolk Council and Norfolk county councillor for Keswick, said he will formally object to the proposed facility, which would require 150MW of electricity and is located close to nature sites including Marston Marsh. Daniel Elmer, Conservative leader of South Norfolk Council He said: “This has got to go through the proper processes and be examined in accordance with the law. But my personal view, is that it is just too damned big for the site it would be on. “It is right next to the marshes and the southern edge of Norwich, while it is near a listed church. “That’s the southern gateway into the city of Norwich. I think you have to think, in terms of the Norwich ‘brand’, what visitors to the city would see when they travel down that road. An aerial view of where the data centre could be built “What they see needs to be aesthetically pleasing and I am not sure that is what they will get given the application which has been submitted at the moment.” The data centre would be two storeys high, while there are also plans for a three-storey office block and a substation. Mr Elmer added: “For this to have any chance of support, it would need to be significantly smaller and lower.” The area where the data centre could be built The Tory leader of the council, which will have the final say on the plans, said he intends to speak against it when it comes before members of his council’s planning committee. The developer says the data centre will create between 100 and 150 jobs and support the demand for data and connectivity fuelled by the rise of artificial intelligence. articles.title: What a Flávio Bolsonaro victory could mean for Brazil, the Amazon and Latin America
articles.desc: A Flávio Bolsonaro presidency could bring tighter fiscal policy at home, closer ties with Washington and a more development-focused approach to the Amazon, with wider implications for Latin America.
articles.content: What a Flávio Bolsonaro victory could mean for Brazil, the Amazon and Latin America | The Business Standard What a Flávio Bolsonaro victory could mean for Brazil, the Amazon and Latin America Last modified: 07 October, 2026, 06:15 pm Flavio Bolsonaro beats expectations in Brazil presidential vote, faces Lula in runoff US, Australia suspend consular services in Brazil Bangladesh, Brazil discuss ways to deepen bilateral cooperation Brazil's Lula bans online betting, unveils debt relief plan as reelection race tightens 20-metre dinosaur fossil unearthed at construction site in Brazil A Flávio Bolsonaro presidency could bring tighter fiscal policy at home, closer ties with Washington and a more development-focused approach to the Amazon, with wider implications for Latin America. Last modified: 07 October, 2026, 06:15 pm Brazil's presidential election has become much more than a contest between an ageing left-wing incumbent and the son of a former far-right president. A victory by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on 25 October could reshape Brazil's economic policy, its approach to the Amazon, its relationship with the United States and China, and the balance of political forces across Latin America. Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, unexpectedly finished first in the 4 October first round with 47.03% of the valid votes, narrowly ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 45.16%. The result overturned expectations that Lula would lead the first round and has made Flávio the favourite heading into the runoff. Keep updated, follow The Business Standard's Google news channel Flávio Bolsonaro's economic agenda calls for a smaller state, tighter control of public spending and a new fiscal framework linked to Brazil's debt-to-GDP ratio. His campaign has pledged a fiscal adjustment of about 1.5% of GDP within 18 months, alongside spending cuts, privatisations and tax relief. On crime, Flávio proposes designating major criminal factions as "narcoterrorist" organisations, expanding federal security spending, building maximum-security prisons and lowering the age of criminal responsibility. His programme also proposes limiting the Supreme Court's powers, including its original criminal jurisdiction over federal lawmakers and individual justices' ability to issue monocratic decisions. He has also said he would seek amnesty for his father, Jair Bolsonaro, and others convicted over the January 2023 attacks on Brazil's government institutions. Flávio has pledged to maintain social programmes such as Bolsa Família, while arguing that welfare should be accompanied by measures to help beneficiaries move into employment. On the environment, he has promised to eliminate illegal deforestation by 2029. At the same time, his programme calls for expanded oil and gas production, the use of fracking and faster, more flexible environmental licensing. That raises questions about how the deforestation target would be reconciled with his broader development agenda. Lula's platform is centred on expanding social protection and public services. His programme proposes maintaining the minimum-wage policy, replacing the six-day workweek with a 40-hour week without a pay cut and strengthening the public healthcare system. He also proposes creating a Ministry of Public Security. On fiscal policy, Lula's approach is more gradual. His campaign has proposed a primary surplus target of 1.3% of GDP by 2030, while seeking to protect social programmes and raise taxes on higher earners. Flávio's camp, by contrast, advocates a much faster adjustment, targeting roughly 1.5% of GDP within 18 months through spending cuts and a new debt-based fiscal rule. The striking point is that Lula is not presiding over an economic collapse. Brazil's economy grew 2% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, while unemployment stood at 5.3% in the June-August period. His problem is therefore less about a single disastrous economic indicator and more about the gap betwee

articles.title: Govt plans 10-year urban development strategy for cities, upazilas: Minister
articles.desc: Zakaria Taher says master plans will initially target metropolitan cities before expanding to large cities and upazilas.
articles.content: Govt plans 10-year city-specific urban development drive: Housing minister | The Business Standard Govt plans 10-year city-specific urban development drive: Housing minister Last modified: 07 October, 2026, 09:52 pm Rajuk plans to approve building plans within 24 days: Housing minister None will be allowed to construct buildings beyond approved design in future: Zakaria July fighters risked lives to 'free Bangladesh again': Housing minister PM stresses integrated urban planning for sustainable water management 101 parks to be constructed in country: Housing minister Master plans to expand from metropolitan cities to upazilas. Last modified: 07 October, 2026, 09:52 pm Six new development authorities already established Dhaka lacks reliable population data for planning Building regulations to target unapproved construction Energy planning urged before urban development The government is preparing a 10-year urban development plan covering metropolitan cities, large cities and eventually upazilas, Housing and Public Works Minister Zakaria Taher said today (7 October). Keep updated, follow The Business Standard's Google news channel Bangladesh needs city-specific master plans and stronger development authorities to manage rapid urbanisation and unplanned construction, he said at the Smart City Conclave 2026 organised by Bonik Barta at Sheraton Dhaka in Banani. Taher said, "Through the Urban Development Directorate (UDD), we have taken a plan for the first time that spans nearly 10 years. "Under this plan, we are initially working with metropolitan cities. Then, starting from large cities, we will work to prepare proper master plans even at the upazila level. We will undertake zoning where what should be located. "We want to work precisely. That is why we are strengthening the UDD," he added. The government has established six new development authorities over the past seven months, covering Mymensingh, Sylhet, Cumilla, Narayanganj, Rangpur and Barishal, the minister said. Four development authorities already existed, while work is also underway to establish one for Bogura, he said. "Without a development authority, we see city corporations themselves providing plans and carrying out the work. There is no check and balance there. We are trying to bring everyone under a comprehensive legal framework," he added. The government is also preparing regulations for buildings constructed without approved plans or in violation of approved plans. "A regulation is being prepared. Work is underway on it. It may go to the cabinet within a month," Taher said, adding that its approval would strengthen the law and increase supervision. Rajuk Chairman Md Riazul Islam said reliable population data remained a major challenge to planning Dhaka. "We know the capital, the DAP area and the available facilities. But in reality, we do not know how many people live here. Some say two crore, some say three crore," he said. He said planners also had to consider daily migration to Dhaka and the growth of new slums. "We cannot prepare plans here based on the models of Europe, America or Australia. They have sufficient land, and they have all kinds of facilities. We have to prepare plans based on the reality of our country," he said. Energy planning needed alongside urban growth East Coast Group Chairman Azam J Chowdhury called for energy infrastructure to be planned alongside urban development. "Before developing each sector, there needs to be an energy plan for it," he said. He proposed treating different sectors of a city as a single development cluster, with a central LPG storage facility supplying households through connections instead of cylinders. Other sessions discussed domestic construction capacity, smart and green housing, housing finance, sustainable urbanisation, and the potential of LPG and solar power. The day-long conclave brought together policymakers, planners, engineers, experts, businesses and representatives of public and private organisation

articles.title: The KFC Open House prototype just may be the spark the brand needs
articles.desc: Marketing Bites: The new restaurant is a testing ground for U.S. President Catherine Tan-Gillespie's turnaround plan, and the Go Bucket launch is just the beginning.
articles.content: The KFC Open House prototype just may be the spark the brand needs Ryan Poli of Iggy’s in Nashville gets ready to open a steakhouse called Claymore How responsible are manufacturers for the end-life of their product? KFC's Open House prototype, outside of Dallas, serves as a testing ground for new ways to "AUV Maxx" as President Catherine Tan-Gillespie describes | Photo courtesy of KFC which made its debut last month just outside of Dallas , is certainly pretty. There are oversized glass windows letting in a ton of Texas sunlight. There are also warm timber accents and plenty of greenery, including succulents and trees, to blend the indoor seating with the patio and the breezeway. It’s also quite modern, with digital boards showcasing menu items, an immersive photo booth experience, a swag bar with merch, and more. But such modernization doesn’t water down the legacy of the brand, which is embraced with signature bucket décor, “Finger Lickin’ Good” slogans and (founder) Colonel Sanders’ signature throughout the restaurant. Though the new restaurant just may indicate that it’s a new day at KFC — which is in the middle of an aggressive turnaround plan led by President Catherine Tan-Gillespie who has been in the role just over a year — we won’t likely see this concept proliferate throughout the country or replace the existing some-3,500 existing domestic restaurants. Rather the point, according to Tan-Gillespie, is to find ways to “AUV Maxx” — and not just to squeeze as much revenue out of its 3,400-square feet as possible, but to find out what is doing the squeezing. Is it the merch? The simplified menu freeing up some employees’ time to focus more on guests? The double drive-thru lane or dedicated delivery driver pickup area? Is it the (brand's-first) breakfast menu? Or, it could be beverages, part of a new lineup called KFC Sips that is similar to the brand’s Kwench beverage platform in several global markets. The point, in other words, is to find what, out of all of these ideas, works and then translate it beyond in KFC’s quest to turn around recent sales declines and market share erosion. Such “AUV-maxxing” is exactly the spark that KFC needs at this moment as the chicken category continues to fill with sexy new startups and legacy burger chains shift their focus (and investment dollars) to the protein. Without such a goal, KFC will remain stagnant, or worse. Consider that in 2025, the chain’s average unit volumes were $1.3 million. That’s essentially the same as they were in 2022 and just $300,000 more than 10 years ago. Notably, the food-away-from-home inflation index rose roughly 46% in those 10 years, while labor increased by about 65%. KFC’s AUVs are lower (and significantly in many cases) than all of its QSR chicken category peers with the exception of Church’s Texas Chicken, according to Technomic. Tan-Gillespie’s comeback plan has so far found plenty of traction with four straight quarters of positive same-store sales, but to really turn around its recent struggles, KFC has to find a way to “maxx” that AUV number to even think about getting back to growth again. Open House is a catalyst to do so and, to the benefit of franchisees, corporate is footing the bill for the prototype because it believes so strongly that it is the best way to truly understand what customers want — not what they say they want, but what they actually want. (Longtime operators are painfully aware that those two things don’t always align). This week, we saw the first element from Open House translate to the broader system with , a snack-sized option with the choice of nuggets, wings or a tender alongside fries or wedges that fits into car cupholders. Consumers clearly want more snack options. According to Datassential, 87% of American consumers now report snacking outside of mealtimes. Snacking also fits tidily into the growing trend of GLP-1 users, which now include nearly 20% of U.S. households. The Go Bucket has worked in international marke

articles.title: US 30-year mortgage rate hits highest in nearly three years
articles.desc: Surge fuelled by growing worries over pressure from soaring oil prices and stronger economic growth.
articles.content: US 30-year mortgage rate hits highest in three years | The Straits Times US 30-year mortgage rate hits highest in nearly three years Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate hit 7.49% last week, severely hurting Americans’ affordability. The average US 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 7.49%, its highest in nearly three years, making homes less affordable for buyers. Higher Treasury yields, oil prices, and stronger growth pushed borrowing costs up. Inflation also rose to 3.4% in August, above the Fed's 2% target. Mortgage applications fell 4.2% last week. The MBA said few homeowners want to refinance, and many buyers are stepping back from the market. The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to its highest in almost three years, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if President Donald Trump’s Republicans keep control of Congress. The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage surged 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended Oct 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) said on Oct 7. It was last higher in November 2023. Mortgage rates are tied closely to the yield on US 10-year Treasury notes, which earlier this week , driven by worries over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth. The cost of living is the top issue on Americans’ minds as they decide how they will vote on Nov 3, a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Oct 5 showed, and is one reason why Trump’s approval rating is at a record ‌low of 32%. Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, which topped 5.3% on Oct 5. Inflation is also on the rise, registering 3.4% in August by a measure that the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. Fed policymakers have signalled they expect to follow their September interest-rate increase with another hike by year’s end, though markets are for now betting at their upcoming policy meeting at the end of October. Mortgage loan applications fell 4.2% last week from the previous week, the MBA said on Oct 7, with refinancing applications dropping sharply. Overall application volumes are the lowest since February 2025 and have fallen nearly 50% since January. “Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market,” said Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist. articles.content: Fact-Check: Israeli Leader Yair Lapid Did Not Say Netanyahu Copied Modi’s Playbook Israeli Leader Yair Lapid Did Not Say Netanyahu Copied PM Modi’s Playbook We found out that the original video of Yair Lapid was altered using AI. A video was shared on social media, claiming to show Israeli Leader of the Opposition, , stating that the Prime Minister of Israel, In the video, Yair Lapid can be heard saying, "Netanyahu is taking a page from Modi's political playbook. In India, Modi used 2019 attack as election campaign to frame political narrative against Pakistan." The FlyDubai incident refers to the recent incident in which a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was forced to divert to Tabuk following an altercation between the two pilots. We ran a reverse image search on the video using Google Lens and found the original video, uploaded by the official YouTube account of is titled "Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid slams Netanyahu for 'total failure' in Iran" In the video, Yair Lapid states that the campaign in Iran was not a success and that Benjamin Netanyahu has led them into a strategic collapse. He also says that the Israeli Prime Minister has deceived the citizens of Israel with a strategic plan that didn't exist and turned something that could have been a military success into a political disaster. , an AI detection tool, which flagged it as more than 99 percent likely to contain AI-generated speech. , an AI detection tool, and found that four of its detectors flagged the viral clip as containing AI-generated content. articles.title: Indian researchers develop metal‑free catalyst to replace platinum to cut clean‑energy costs
articles.desc: Digital Desk | New Delhi, Oct 7 (IANS) A team of Indian researchers developed a metal‑free porous material that can perform nearly as well as platinum as a catalyst in zinc‑air batteries that can significantly lower costs for next‑generation clean‑energy technologies, the government said on Wednesda
articles.content: Digital Desk | New Delhi, Oct 7 (IANS) A team of Indian researchers developed a metal‑free porous material that can perform nearly as well as platinum as a catalyst in zinc‑air batteries that can significantly lower costs for next‑generation clean‑energy technologies, the government said on Wednesday. The material, named TTT‑DHTD and built from abundant elements including carbon, sulfur, nitrogen and hydrogen, forms an ultra‑porous honeycomb‑like network that efficiently converts oxygen into electricity, an official statement said. "Laboratory tests showed that the new catalyst achieved about 96 per cent of the performance of commercial platinum catalysts, while remaining remarkably stable," the statement from the Ministry of Science & Technology said. Even after 120 hours of continuous operation, the material maintained its performance without the degradation or contamination that often affects conventional metal-based catalysts. Compared with hydrogen fuel cells, Zn–air batteries can provide a simpler, more compact energy storage solution that does not require high-pressure hydrogen storage or extensive hydrogen infrastructure, the statement noted. However, both Zn–air batteries and hydrogen fuel cells critically rely on efficient oxygen electrochemistry. Currently, many clean-energy technologies, particularly hydrogen fuel cells, depend on platinum, one of the world’s rarest and most expensive metals, as an efficient ORR catalyst. “While platinum provides excellent catalytic performance, its high cost, scarcity and limited availability remain major barriers to large-scale deployment,” the ministry said, stressing the need for platinum-free ORR catalysts. The newly developed material has an engineered molecular structure that creates ideal sites where oxygen molecules can readily attach and react, enabling electricity to be generated quickly and efficiently. Replacing platinum with inexpensive organic materials could dramatically reduce the cost of Zn-air cells, making clean transportation, portable power systems, and renewable energy storage more affordable and accessible. “By combining innovative molecular design with advanced computational studies, the researchers have demonstrated that earth-abundant materials can rival the performance of precious metals in one of the most important reactions for clean-energy technologies,” the statement noted.

The ancient reptile was identified in the historical records as belonging to the genus Tomistoma, the “false gharial.” The problem is that the only false gharials living today exist some 5,000 miles away, in the freshwaters of Malaysia and Indonesia. And while it’s possible to imagine that at some point in the last 50 million years this fish-hunting reptile made its way across deserts, mountain ranges, tropics and oceans, Paul Burke, a postdoctoral paleontology research fellow at the Swedish Museum of Natural History, proposed a different explanation. As a PhD student, Burke investigated the several dozen named gharial species that had gone extinct, piecing together their evolutionary history based on their braincases (and brains, by extrapolation). Based on the morphology of the skull, the two weren’t really closely related. Working with CT scans, Burke and a team of international researchers compared over 300 data points on the size and shape of the skull of the Egyptian creature with that of other gharials (both living and extinct). Their findings, published Tuesday in the journal Royal Society Open Science, concluded that this was a distinct species never before identified. “Not to discredit the work that people did in the past – because they did great work for the time – but they would make very generic statements,” Burke said in an interview from Stockholm. “They say something like ‘nasal bone, long or short?’ That’s very subjective.” Within the last decade, thanks to a combination of scanning technology, a larger database of samples and a more advanced understanding of biological morphology, such assessments have become much more refined. Take the nasal bone. The way it is now used in classification might involve asking dozens of questions: Is the nasal bone twice as long as the jaw bone, for example? articles.desc: The Royal Swedish Academy honors groundbreaking research that uses South Pole ice to trace mysterious cosmic rays back to their violent origins.
articles.content: The 2026 Nobel Prize: Meet the 'Ghost Particles' Passing Through You Right Now The 2026 Nobel Prize: Meet the 'Ghost Particles' Passing Through You Right Now The Royal Swedish Academy honors groundbreaking research that uses South Pole ice to trace mysterious cosmic rays back to their violent origins. Inside the Super-Kamiokande neutrino detector during work on the detectors.Credit: Kamioka Observatory, ICRR, Univ. Tokyo The universe is full of particles that we cannot see, and some of them are passing through your body right now. They are called neutrinos, and they are so difficult to detect that physicists have nicknamed them “ These elusive cosmic messengers are at the centre of the in Physics, awarded to Belgian-American physicist Francis Halzen. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences honoured Halzen for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and his groundbreaking discovery of high-energy neutrinos originating from deep cosmic sources. Operating under a cubic kilometre of clear Antarctic ice at the South Pole, IceCube acts as a massive particle trap. Halzen’s visionary leadership transformed this frozen expanse into the world's largest neutrino telescope. By capturing the rare, faint blue light emitted when neutrinos collide with ice atoms, his work opened a brand-new window into the high-energy universe. The Nobel committee emphasized that Halzen’s discoveries have fundamentally reshaped modern astrophysics. His research allows scientists to trace these "ghosts" back to violent cosmic events, such as supermassive black holes and exploding stars, solving century-old mysteries about the origins of cosmic rays.
